messages.subject: lavaan function + estimator = "MLM"
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to run a CFA using the lavaan function. This is my code:

congeneric.model <- '#latent variable
                      WMC =~ 1*DS_pun_b1 + DS_pun_b2 + DS_pun_b3 + DS_pun_b4 + DS_pun_b5
                      
                     #residual variances of observed variables
                      DS_pun_b1 ~~ DS_pun_b1
                      DS_pun_b2 ~~ DS_pun_b2
                      DS_pun_b3 ~~ DS_pun_b3
                      DS_pun_b4 ~~ DS_pun_b4
                      DS_pun_b5 ~~ DS_pun_b5

                     #factor variance(s)
                      WMC ~~ WMC

                     #factor covariance(s)
                      '
fit <- lavaan(congeneric.model,
                    data=dat, 
                    estimator="ML")

and my results

> show(fit)
lavaan (0.5-17) converged normally after  52 iterations

  Number of observations                           200

  Estimator                                                  ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic               7.472
  Degrees of freedom                                  5
  P-value (Chi-square)                                0.188

However, when I'm trying to use estimator = "MLM", my results are:

> show(fit)
lavaan (0.5-17) converged normally after  59 iterations

  Number of observations                           200

  Estimator                                                 ML             Robust
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              695.545     782.473
  Degrees of freedom                                10               10
  P-value (Chi-square)                               0.000        0.000
  Scaling correction factor                                          0.889
    for the Satorra-Bentler correction

When I'm using the cfa function and MLM estimator, my results are:

> show(fit)
lavaan (0.5-17) converged normally after  52 iterations

  Number of observations                           200

  Estimator                                                   ML      Robust
  Minimum Function Test Statistic                7.472       7.344
  Degrees of freedom                                   5              5
  P-value (Chi-square)                                 0.188       0.196
  Scaling correction factor                                           1.017
    for the Satorra-Bentler correction

which are equivalent to results I get from Mplus. My question is: Is the lavaan function not supposed to do simple CFAs under the MLM estimator option? Or am I doing anything wrong?
Philipp

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: lavaan function + estimator = "MLM"
parts:
Look at the mean structure parameters in the Lavaan and cfa solutions.  My guess is that the lavaan solution has the intercepts for your 5 observed variables fixed at 0, while the CFA solution has them as free parameters.  Hence the differences in DF and fit.  Remember, the lavaan functions has minimal helpful defaults.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan function + estimator = "MLM"
parts:
On 10/27/2014 11:18 AM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> Look at the mean structure parameters in the Lavaan and cfa solutions.
> My guess is that the lavaan solution has the intercepts for your 5
> observed variables fixed at 0, while the CFA solution has them as free
> parameters. Hence the differences in DF and fit. Remember, the lavaan
> functions has minimal helpful defaults.

Acknowledged. The MLM estimator requires a meanstructure, and if you are
using the lavaan() function, you need to provide all the required model
parameters (including these means).

If you prefer a more user-friendly approach, use the cfa() or sem()
functions.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan function + estimator = "MLM"
parts:
On 10/27/2014 12:46 PM, phitho29 wrote:
> Hi Ed,
>
> thanks for your reply. I'm still confused: My results change dependent
> on the estimator I use. As I understand it, df's should not change when
> switching between ML and MLM estimation? In both cases, I'm using the
> lavaan function. The only thing I'm changing is the estimator (from ML
> to MLM). Why do the df's change?

Because MLM requires a meanstructure, while ML does not. And although
the lavaan() function will add model parameters for the means, they are
-by default- fixed to zero. If you allow them to be free, the df's will
be the same again.

Yves.
